name: media-split-section
purpose: One claim beside its picture, on its own frame: the copy cell with its overline, headline and sentence on one side, and the media on a raised, pixel-textured surface on the other. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'media-split-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, a framed `media-split`, `button`, `illustration`, `console-mockup` and the webkit scene assets. The media is required and is a drawn asset: an illustration (a name of the illustration registry) or a registered scene, of which a product console widget (`widget`) is one; request-flow diagrams and code do not go in a media band; with one action the whole band links to it (unless `linked` is off), with two the band stays unlinked. The media sits beside the copy, or under it when `orientation` is `vertical`.
useWhen: Rendering page JSON, or you need a whole band with no custom content → the section (`media-split-section`). Building an SFC by hand, needing slots, or nesting inside another band → the primitive (`media-split`).
Use MediaSplitSection for one marketing claim beside its picture or scene.
To make one point beside one picture and move on (a values statement, a single product claim).
avoidWhen: For several claims stacked one after the other → use `media-split-stack-section`.
For a claim beside the code that delivers it → use `feature-scroll-section` (each item's `code`); a media band shows no code.
For a request-flow diagram → use `console-showcase-section` with `variant: 'diagram'` (the diagram as its `scene`) or `architecture-tabs-section`; a media band shows no diagram.
For a full-width terminal session with no copy column → use `cli-terminal-section`.
For copy beside one piece of media in a hand-built SFC that needs the `media` slot → use `media-split`.
related: `media-split` — the band primitive the section is rendered with.
`media-split-stack-section` — the stacked sibling for a run of claims.
bestPractices: Give the band exactly one media: `scene`, `widget` (a `ConsoleMockup` name) or `illustration` (a registry name); when several are set the first of that order wins. A band with a title and no media logs a development warning, and the site-composition check (`test/standards/site-composition.test.mjs`) fails it in the shipped page JSON. A `Diagram` scene counts as no media.
Use `size="large"` for a band that carries only its headline and description.
Use `orientation="vertical"` for a wide scene that needs the full width of the frame under the copy.
Turn `linked` off when the media holds controls of its own, so a click in it is not taken as a click on the band.
Set `anchor` when another part of the page links to the band.
Name a registry scene in `illustration` for art; the band takes no picture URL.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered by the media split as its `h2` and naming its region; the band renders nothing when empty.

props.name: size
props.doc: Type scale of the copy; `large` sets the headline at heading-xl and centres the copy beside the media, `medium` aligns it to the top of the media.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Axis the band splits on; `vertical` stacks the media under the copy for a wide scene.

props.name: texture
props.doc: Texture painted under the media: `dots`, `grid`, `lines`, `dither`, `pixelate` or `none`.

props.name: linked
props.doc: Links the whole band to a lone action; turn it off when the media holds controls of its own.

props.name: scene
props.doc: Scene drawn in the media cell, `{ component, props? }` naming a webkit scene asset other than `Diagram` and the props bound onto it; wins over every other media.

props.name: widget
props.doc: Name of the product console widget drawn in the media cell when no scene is set.

props.name: illustration
props.doc: Registry name of the illustration drawn in the media cell when neither a scene nor a widget is set.

props.name: illustrationAriaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the illustration; empty keeps it decorative.

props.name: primaryAction
props.doc: First button under the copy; `{ label, href, trailing?, icon?, target?, variant? }`. When it is the only action it renders outlined with a trailing chevron, and the whole band links to it; `variant` overrides the drawn variant.

props.name: secondaryAction
props.doc: Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, icon?, target?, variant? }`. With two actions the band stays unlinked.
